evidence_jobs.title: Enrollment Manager (District Enrollment, Recruitment & Student Records Manager)
evidence_jobs.quote: Ensure that the academy teams maintain accurate student records in the school's Student Information System (PowerSchool), including but not limited to demographic, guardian, and emergency contact information, free & reduced lunch status, and coding of student indicators (ELL, SPED, etc.)

evidence_jobs.title: Enrollment Manager (Paylocity posting, same req)
evidence_jobs.quote: Publish enrollment and demographic data to WISEdata and resolve data validation errors such as missing documentation, duplicate records, or inactive students.

talk_track: I work as a fractional CTO giving independent and charter school boards a straight answer to "where is our technology risk?" -- without replacing the IT people already in the building. Your open Enrollment Manager role asks one person to "maintain accurate student records in the school's Student Information System (PowerSchool)" while also publishing to WISEdata and running offers through SchoolMint. Read plainly, that puts custody documents, medical alerts, immunization records and household income data across three vendor systems under a manager reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, with no technology executive above them on your staff directory. I watched two schools take the same vendor breach: the one with a governance layer was back in days, the other spent weeks explaining itself to families. For a board that meets every other month, the useful artifact isn't a new system -- it's one page naming which vendor holds what, and who answers when it leaks. Worth putting on the next board agenda?

notes.edp_caveat: MAS is publicly funded (97% free/reduced lunch), not tuition-funded, so Kenneth's tuition-attrition framing does not transfer literally; the enrollment-revenue link still holds via per-pupil state funding, which is exactly why the Enrollment Manager role exists.
